faqs.q: What should I include on an auto detailing invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name, the client and vehicle details (make, model, VIN), a dated line-item list of services (wash & wax, interior, coating, polish), tax, and a total due. Record the VIN so each car's history stays clear.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Is this the same as a car detailing invoice template?
faqs.a: Yes. Car detailing invoice and auto detailing invoice refer to the same document. This template includes pre-filled line items for exterior wash, interior detail, wax, ceramic coating, and engine bay cleaning - use it for any car or auto detailing service.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your tax authority and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: Detailing invoices: packages, stages and mobile premiums
deepDive.sub: Detailing is sold as packages but priced by process. The invoice needs both, because the package name is what the customer bought and the process is what justifies the price.

blocks.h3: Package tiers and what separates them
paras: An exterior wash and a full interior detail are different products, and the price gap is not a markup — it is hours. A basic wash and vacuum is one to two hours; a full interior and exterior detail is four to six; a paint correction is a full day or more. If the invoice only says 'full detail', the customer has no way to see why the next tier costs twice as much.

The package names vary by shop, which is fine, but the invoice line should carry a short description of what was included: decontamination and clay, interior steam and extraction, engine bay, headlight restoration. Those descriptions are also what the customer compares when they shop your price against someone else's.

blocks.h3: Paint correction is billed by stage, not by car
paras: A one-step polish removes light swirls and improves gloss. A two-step adds a cutting stage and removes deeper defects, and takes roughly twice as long. A ceramic coating is priced on top because the surface preparation is the labour, and a coating applied over uncorrected paint is a warranty claim waiting to happen.

Invoice correction as its own line with the stage stated, and note the condition assessment that justified it. 'Two-stage correction required due to automatic car wash swirls' is a defensible invoice. A single big number is a negotiation.

blocks.h3: The mobile premium and its conditions
paras: Mobile detailing carries a travel charge — commonly $25 to $75 within a service radius — and requires water and power access that the customer may not have. A mobile job without a water source means the detailer brings a tank and a generator, which is a different, higher price.

Put the access requirement on the invoice and on the booking confirmation: 'customer to provide water spigot and 120V outlet'. When neither is available on arrival, the honest invoice is a trip charge, and having stated the requirement in advance is what makes it collectable.
steps: Confirm vehicle condition and take photos before starting.
Note any pre-existing damage on the invoice.
State the correction stage used and why.
Bill travel as a separate line where the job is mobile.
State the coating cure time and the wash restrictions that follow it.

paras: A deposit of 20 to 50 percent is standard for correction and coating work because the slot is long and hard to fill at short notice. State the cancellation window — typically 48 hours — and what is retained if it is missed. A no-show policy that only exists in conversation is not a policy.
